newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Kia seeks to boost car sales.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Kia seeks to boost car sales.

text.p: South Korea's Kia Motors, facing lacklustre local sales, hopes to lure consumers with a slew of new models in the months ahead, company officials said on Thursday.
"New cars, we hope, will revive consumer interest again," said spokesman Chun Sang-jin.
Kia, the country's second largest car maker, would introduce an upgrade of its sub-compact Sephia mid-year, a new mini-van and a mid-sized sedan in the second half, he said.
The new Sephia will compete with Daewoo Motor's Nubira, now the bestseller in the 1.5- to 1.8-litre segment of the market, and Hyundai Motor's Avante.
"The planned model changes look timely. They will significantly boost Kia's sales," said Hur Kang, analyst at Hyundai Securities.
Last month, Kia replaced its flagship Potentia luxury sedan with the Enterprise, now South Korea's largest car.
"We hope the mini-van, aimed at defeating Hyundai's Starex, will become popular," Chun said.
South Korea's domestic car sales have been hit by a slowing economy, which has forced consumers to cut back spending on durable goods.
Kia's domestic sales during the January-March period plunged 36 percent to 70,684 vehicles from 110,597 in the year-earlier period.
"Domestic sales will meet our target of 500,000 units this year with the help of new models," Chun said.
The company's domestic sales totaled 458,000 vehicles in 1996. Total sales were 781,250.
Kia also said it planned to set up a specialised marketing company in April or May to increase local sales.
"The new company will be responsible for car sales and after-sales service. It will help Kia Motors focus on production and research," said Min Jae-ki, another Kia spokesman.
Kia said it was considering absorbing Kia Service Co Ltd, which now provides after-sales service, into the new company.
Company officials said Kia needed to strengthen its marketing capability, which compares unfavourably with that of rivals Hyundai Motor and Daewoo Motor.
Kia's domestic sales in March fell 19.5 percent to 28,378 units with sales of its sub-compact Avella and Sephia models battered by Daewoo's new models.
Daewoo began selling its sub-compact Lanos last November and larger model Nubira in February.
Avella sales in the local market plunged to 1,227 vehicles in March from 2,791 units a year earlier, while Sephia sales tumbled to 4,834 from 7,806, Kia said.
